description_full: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. produces and sells products in cooking, serving, cleanup, and storage, and tableware product categories in the United States and internationally. The company operates through four segments: Reynolds Cooking & Baking, Hefty Waste & Storage, Hefty Tableware, and Presto Products. The Reynolds Cooking & Baking segment produces aluminum foil, disposable aluminum pans, parchment paper, freezer paper, wax paper, butcher paper, plastic wrap, baking cups, oven bags, and slow cooker liners under the Reynolds Wrap, Reynolds Kitchens, and EZ Foil brands in the United States, as well as under the ALCAN brand in Canada and under the Diamond brand internationally. The Hefty Waste & Storage segment offers trash and food storage bags under the Hefty Ultra Strong and Hefty Strong brands; and food storage bags under the Hefty brands. It also provides a suite of products, including compostable bags, bags made from recycled materials. The Hefty Tableware segment offers disposable and compostable plates, bowls, platters, containers, cups, and cutlery under the Hefty brand, as well as dishes and party cups. The Presto Products segment primarily sells store brand products in food storage bags, trash bags, and plastic wrap categories. It offers both branded and store brand products to grocery stores, mass merchants, warehouse clubs, discount chains, dollar stores, drug stores, home improvement stores, military outlets, and eCommerce retailers. Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. was founded in 1947 and is headquartered in Lake Forest, Illinois. Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. is a subsidiary of Packaging Finance Limited.

financial_summary: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $5.1B market cap on $3.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.

Returns on capital run at 10% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 25% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $316M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.58× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 5.6×.

Shareholder yield of 3.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 74% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

growth: Revenue has compounded at -0.8% over 3 years and 2.7% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.
